pool.text: The red sandstone Münster was badly damaged in the great earthquake.
The University of Basel, Switzerland's oldest university, was established in the city.
Basel officially joined the Swiss Confederacy as its eleventh canton.
The public museum collection was first created back in Europe.
A short civil war led the disadvantaged countryside to secede from Basel.
Switzerland's first zoo opened its doors in the south of Basel.
The Schola Cantorum Basiliensis was founded as a worldwide research centre.
The psychedelic drug LSD was first synthesized by Albert Hofmann in Basel.
The local population voted to buy three Pablo Picasso works of art.
Ernst Beyeler founded Art Basel as an important contemporary art fair.
The Paul Sacher Foundation opened and houses a major manuscript collection.
The Basel Convention was opened for signature to prevent hazardous waste exports.
The European Festival of Youth Choirs started as a Basel tradition.
The city of Basel received the Wakker Prize.
Basel contended to become the European Capital of Culture.
Theater Basel was chosen as the best stage for German performances.
A building construction law was passed mandating green flat roofs in Basel.
The fifth European Festival of Youth Choirs opened in Basel.
Basel Tattoo was founded by the local Top Secret Drum Corps.
Switzerland joined the Schengen Area, ending immigration checks at the crossings.
